name: Delacroix house
status: proposed (address and placement); design from the author's film still (reference/lori-house.webp), detail from reference/board-17.jpg and board-19.jpg
materials: warm red-brown brick in Flemish bond with darker burnt headers, light mortar
darker brick base with a limestone water table
dark natural slate hipped roof with lead hip and ridge caps, copper valleys
white painted dentil cornice, pediment, pilasters, portico and balustrade
black louvered shutters, 6-over-6 white sash windows, arched fanlights
limestone sills, jack-arch lintels and keystones; bluestone terrace and treads
lead-coated copper bay roof, aged copper downspouts
asphalt drive with Belgian-block (granite) edging, brick paver landing and terrace
notes: Main block 18.0 x 11.5 m (x -9..9, y -5.75..5.75), first floor 0.60 m above grade, second floor 4.15 m, cornice soffit 7.2 m, 34 deg slate hip to a 11.9 m ridge; twin corbelled end chimneys to 13.55 m. The Atlas height (8.0 m) is too low for a 2.5-story Georgian house with the tall roof in the photo, so the ridge is about 48% higher. The pavilion projects 1.0 m; the portico, terrace and steps reach y = -10.5 (1.1 m beyond the footprint). Wings make the house about 30 m wide: the 1.5-story front-gabled left wing (x -15..-9) and the two-story hipped right wing (x 9..15). From the photo: brick, dark slate hip, tall corbelled chimney, white columned portico with balustraded balcony, pedimented pavilion with an arched fanlight rising into the pediment, black shutters, front-gabled left wing, the shed-roofed porch between the wing and the portico, lanterns, arched first-floor windows on the right, attic dormers, curving drive. Interpretations: the side, rear and roof plan (rear ell, dormers front and back, side entry, chimney positions), the box bay on the wing (after board-19), Flemish bond, the drive layout (a horseshoe with a planted island and a spur to a parking court at the right wing), gate piers, rear terrace and the three hardwoods. The lot GLB has no lawn; its drive meets the curb line exactly at two flared mouths. The lot owns its frontage: the brick gate piers stand 3.95 m behind the curb line (caps 3.58 m), so nothing walled or hedged sits in the 1.8-3.3 m sidewalk zone; only the drive and its granite edging run to the curb. The three hardwoods (white-oak habit, 16.5-18 m) are a trunk with root flares, scaffold limbs, branches and twigs carrying about 530 small soft leaf clumps each in a lobed crown shell, shaded by vertex colour (darker inside and underneath); no alpha cards.
